expanded_hypotheses: JacobiSolutionOn carries explicit pointwise HasDerivAtR derivative data du, ddu and C¹-on-[a,b] continuity; the ODE is u'' + k·u = 0 on the open interval with the curvature inequality k₂ ≤ k₁ on the closed interval — no smoothness of k is assumed anywhere.

Riccati comparisons require positivity of the solutions u₁, u₂ on the closed interval Icc a b (not merely the open one); this is exactly what makes every denominator bounded away from zero and is the standard no-conjugate-point hypothesis on the finite interval.

The singular Riccati comparisons require continuity of m, m̄ on Ioc 0 T = (0,T] (v2 corrected domain) — continuity on [0,T] would contradict the Euclidean normalization (proved: euclideanNormalizedOn_not_continuousOn_zero). The initial conditions are the quantitative Euclidean normalization |m t − d/t| ≤ C, |m̄ t − d/t| ≤ C on (0,t₀]; for a Jacobi field with u 0 = 0, u' 0 = 1 and bounded u'' this normalization is derivable (documented as the missing bridge lemma; the honest u(0)=0, u'(0)=1 form is the expanded-hypothesis target for the Rauch corollary).

The volume-ratio chain requires: A, Ā C¹ on (0,T) with m = A'/A, m̄ = Ā'/Ā pointwise; A, Ā > 0 on (0,T] (positivity on the correct half-open interval); A, Ā continuous on [0,T]; A 0 = Ā 0 = 0 (areas of the radius-0 sphere); d > 0; 0 < t₀ ≤ T; C ≥ 0; k̄ ≤ k on (0,T). Each hypothesis is exactly the analytic image of a standard Bishop-Gromov hypothesis; none is equivalent to the conclusion (the Euclidean model satisfies all of them and the conclusion is not trivially forced for non-model data).
Non-vacuity is witnessed by the Euclidean model m = d/t, A = t^d with k = k̄ = 0, C = 0 (ModelEuclidean.lean), including the explicit volume V t = t^(d+1)/(d+1).

semantic_class.volume_ratio: conditional analytic — bishopGromovVolumeRatio is proved for density functions A, Ā under fully expanded analytic hypotheses; it becomes the geometric Bishop-Gromov theorem exactly when A is identified with the (n−1)-volume of geodesic spheres, which is the remaining geometric construction
semantic_class.models: non-vacuity witnesses — Euclidean model instances of the singular comparisons and of the full chain

remaining_blockers: GEOMETRIC BRIDGE (missing construction, not assumed anywhere): for a complete Riemannian manifold with radial sectional curvatures (or Ric) bounded below by (n−1)K, prove that the (n−1)-volume density A t of the geodesic spheres satisfies A'/A = tr S/(n−1) with the shape-operator Riccati equation S' + S² + R_γ = 0 and the Cauchy-Schwarz step tr S² ≥ (tr S)²/(n−1), hence m' + m²/d + K ≤ 0 and the Euclidean normalization near 0. Needs a Riemannian-geometry framework (exponential map, Jacobi fields, sphere measures) — not present in the release package; upstream candidates: MorganTian/DoCarmo/LeeLib in third_party/frenzymath (book formalizations, not Lean proofs).

MODEL VOLUME CONSTANT: the geometric model volume is V̄ t = ω_{n−1}·∫₀ᵗ j_K(s)^(n−1) ds where ω_{n−1} is the measure of the Euclidean unit (n−1)-sphere; a mathlib API check for that constant is still open. All D12 volume-ratio statements are scale-free (ratios), so the constant cancels; it is needed only for absolute volume statements.

RAUCH COROLLARY BRIDGE: the one-sided Rauch corollaries u ≤ j_K (k ≥ K) and u ≥ j_K (k ≤ K) for the scalar Jacobi solution u versus the D10 model j_K are the natural next downstream uses of riccati_le/ge_of_singular_normalization with d = 1; missing pieces (planned, not yet proved): (i) the quantitative normalization lemma |u t/t − 1| ≤ B·t and |du t − 1| ≤ B·t from u 0 = 0, du 0 = 1, |ddu| ≤ B (double mean-value theorem); (ii) the model normalization |jacobiSol K t/t − 1| ≤ √|K|·t·(1/6) for K ≥ 0 via abs_sub_sin_le; (iii) the ratio-limit argument u ε/j_K ε → 1. The mirrored singular comparison riccati_ge_of_singular_normalization needed for the lower direction is already proved.

HYPERBOLIC MODEL NORMALIZATION: for K < 0 the quantitative bound |sinh(√(−K)t)/(√(−K)t) − 1| ≤ C·t is not yet formalized (series or convexity bound); the spherical/flat cases suffice for the first Rauch corollary.
next_dependency_requests: Mathlib API check: surface measure / volume of the Euclidean unit sphere S^{n−1} (ω_{n−1}) — needed for the absolute model volume V̄ t = ω_{n−1}·∫₀ᵗ j_K^{n−1}; scale-free ratios do not need it.

Any Riemannian-geometry Lean development with: exponential map, Jacobi fields J'' + R(J,γ')γ' = 0, geodesic sphere (n−1)-measures A t = vol(S_t), and the shape-operator Riccati equation S' + S² + R_γ = 0 — required to promote bishopGromovVolumeRatio from a density-level theorem to the geometric Bishop-Gromov theorem.

D10-side: quantitative small-t bounds for jacobiSol K and jacobiDeriv K (|j_K t/t − 1| and |j_K' t − 1| of order t) — spherical and flat cases have mathlib support (abs_sub_sin_le, one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos); hyperbolic needs a bound on |sinh x − x|.
